subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & US vs EU region costs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom R. <tom.r@acme.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Discovery — token volumes, budget, and region requirements

Tom — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick recap to make sure we captured next steps and a couple of outstanding pricing questions:

- Confirmed expected monthly token volumes: 100M–400M tokens (varies by feature adoption; current pilot ~25M).
- Target unit economics discussed: you mentioned aiming for a cost target in the neighborhood of $X per 1M tokens — I understood this as $600–$900 / 1M tokens depending on QA margin. Please correct me if I misheard.
- Regional/data residency: Acme requires EU data residency for EU customers which may impact per-token cost.

Action items I have:
1) Provide a concise pricing estimate (US region vs EU region) with example unit economics at 100M, 250M, and 400M tokens/mo.
2) Call out quantization/throughput options that affect cost (e.g., 8-bit vs 4-bit variants, batching).
3) Include any SLA/enterprise add-on uplift (private VPC, KMS integration).

I've attached my call notes and a short pricing template. Ben — looping you in to provide the region-specific pricing numbers and an initial $/1M token target we can propose.

Next step from Tom/Priya: confirm the acceptable budget range for pilot and 12-month commit (ballpark is fine).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: MAP-ACME-DiscoveryNotes.docx
From: Tom R. <tom.r@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya S. <priya.s@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery — token volumes, budget, and region requirements

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Volumes: 100M–400M is right as a mid-term expectation. Pilot budget will be small (~25–50M) but we want a clear ramp plan and unit costs for when usage scales.
- Budget: for pilot we can do $10k–$25k/mo. For a committed 12-month plan we can stretch to ~$60k–$90k/mo depending on enterprise discounts and data residency costs.
- Data residency: EU customers must keep data in EU. We need to understand the delta in cost for serving from EU regions vs US (both per-token and any minimum committed spend). Also call out whether EU residency requires Private/VPC deployment or if Hosted with EU-region tenancy suffices.

Can you include a simple table showing: region (US, EU), base $/1M tokens, enterprise uplift %, and example monthly spend at 100M/250M/400M?

Appreciate the fast turn.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Product Integrations | Acme Corp
Tom.R@acme.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom R. <tom.r@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery — token volumes, budget, and region requirements

Tom / Marissa — adding the pricing context below. These are conservative list figures to start the conversation; we can model specific commit tiers and discounts once we know target ARPU and commitment level.

Pricing (list, per 1M tokens):
- US region hosted (standard models): $700 / 1M tokens
- EU region hosted (standard models, EU-residency tenancy): $840 / 1M tokens (20% uplift to cover regional infra and higher cloud costs)
- Dedicated/Private (VPC + KMS): base + 35% uplift on top of region price (includes dedicated GPU pools, network ingress egress controls, and audit logging).

Examples (monthly spend):
- 100M tokens: US = $70k; EU = $84k; Private (EU) = $113.4k
- 250M tokens: US = $175k; EU = $210k; Private (EU) = $283.5k
- 400M tokens: US = $280k; EU = $336k; Private (EU) = $453.6k

Notes on unit economics and levers:
- Model choice & quantization: switching to a 4-bit quantized variant can reduce per-token compute costs ~20–30% (depends on model and perf needs). We can run a short eval to estimate real savings.
- Batching/kv-cache: performance tuning (inference batching, prefix caching) can further drop effective $/1M for chat-heavy patterns by 10–25%.
- Minimums & term: we recommend committing to a 6–12 month reserved capacity model if you want to hit the lower end of the unit cost curve. We can prepare a tiered proposal (e.g., 10% discount at 250M commitment, 20% at 500M).

Marissa — attaching a short PDF with these high-level numbers and a simple spend table you can pass along. Happy to jump on a short call with Tom & Priya to walk tradeoffs.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Pricing | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf
From: Priya S. <priya.s@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom R. <tom.r@acme.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery — token volumes, budget, and region requirements

Thanks Ben — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few follow-ups/questions before we take to procurement:

1) For EU residency: can you confirm whether the hosted EU tenancy option meets our compliance needs (data never leaves EU), or if we should plan for Private (VPC) to meet our auditors? Any customers you can cite who use hosted EU tenancy vs Private?
2) The 20% EU uplift makes sense — can you show a worked example that includes network egress assumptions (we have moderate egress to downstream analytics systems)?
3) Pilot budget: looks like we can do $15k–$20k/mo. For pilot, what mix of model size / quantization would you recommend to stay within that while still showing meaningful results?

If you can turn this into a 1-page proposal with a 3-line summary, the per-region table (US/EU/Private), and recommended pilot config (model + quantization + expected pilot throughput), we'll share with procurement and auditors.

Would like the doc today if possible — can do a quick 20-min sync at 1:30pm PT if you want to walk through.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Sr. Program Manager, Integrations | Acme Corp
priya.s@acme.com
